items.title: Export occurrence-specific supplied forms and preserve product alternatives
items.body:
Generic ingredient mapping must not erase the product/preparation reported by a source. Existing supplied-form and recipe evidence preserves this distinction, but it needs a structured, versioned export for KG-Microbe.

Tracking: https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/767. Depends on https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/768; publish alongside the manifest/annotation contract in https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/769.

## Deliverables and acceptance

- [ ] Define stable source occurrence and supplied-form identifiers, with links to the generic ingredient, source recipe/observation, original label, evidence, supplier, catalog number and known preparation/grade. Preserve source detail and uncertainty without inventing lot identities.
- [ ] Model product alternatives explicitly. Preserve `CultureMech:015191`'s Sigma A9647 **or** A7409 as alternatives, not simultaneous confirmed ingredients, interchangeable identities or a pipe list with unspecified semantics.
- [ ] Retain all seven reviewed BSA recipe memberships and their own amounts/preparation notes. Sigma A7030 belongs only to its reporting source; do not propagate its heat-shock/low-fatty-acid/protease qualifiers to every BSA occurrence.
- [ ] Document when occurrence qualifiers suffice and when a separately identified product/material is required because its identity or associated facts differ. A catalog product, a generic ingredient, a stock solution and an individual lot must not be conflated.
- [ ] Keep supplier/catalog fields out of generic ingredient exact synonyms and identity xrefs. A CAS shared by products does not equate those products; a catalog number alone does not establish molecular identity.
- [ ] Export deterministic source-linked records with an explicit alternatives/unknown-value contract and schema version. Bind them into the common release manifest and existing evidence/review process, with owner and reference validation.
- [ ] Add fixtures for the seven BSA occurrences, A9647-or-A7409, distinct products sharing a CAS, missing product information, and unresolved Sorbitan material. Preserve original source payloads and stable recipe references.

Implementation starts from `supplied_form` in `src/mediaingredientmech/schema/mediaingredientmech.yaml` and the existing occurrence/source evidence; do not overwrite source-specific claims with the shared ingredient's attributes.

Evidence and boundaries: [BSA source review](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/tree/ea697252223774072a188ae3ec23a0e2adea0778/reports/sssom_completion_20260921/mapping_review/identity-review-20260924), [#762](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/762). [#449](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/449) owns the broader recipe-membership import defect; preserve/reuse that work. Sorbitan identity evidence remains under [#761](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/761).

items.title: water_multiplicity misses hyphen-separated hydrates that exist in the data
items.body:
Found while reviewing PR #255 (closes #254).

\`_DIGIT_WATER\` in \`src/mediaingredientmech/curation/hydrate_guard.py\` accepts these separators before a digit multiplier:

\`\`\`
[x × · • ・ ⋅ ∙ . whitespace]
\`\`\`

but **not** the ASCII hyphen \`-\`. Hyphen-separated hydrate labels are present in the corpus:

\`\`\`
ZnSO4-7H2O
CuCl2-2H2O
Na2MoO4-2H2O
\`\`\`

All three parse to \`None\` ("unspecified") today:

\`\`\`
>>> water_multiplicity('ZnSO4-7H2O')  -> None
>>> water_multiplicity('CuCl2-2H2O')  -> None
\`\`\`

Consequence: a \`ZnSO4-7H2O\` synonym sitting on a record labelled e.g. \`ZnSO4 x 6 H2O\` is a genuine hydration-state collapse that the #254 detector silently skips. The direction is safe (false-negative, never a false mismatch), but the miss is real because these strings actually occur.

Fix: add \`-\` (and consider the Unicode minus U+2212) to the separator class, with a pinned test case. Guard against false positives from names like \`omega-3\` — the regex already requires \`(\d+)\s*H2\s*O\` contiguous, so \`-3 fatty acid ... H2O\` will not match.

items.title: Decompose and repair the microbedecoder residual (#213/#308/#313)
items.body:
Answers "is the microbedecoder unmapped mapping complete?" — it was not, and the remainder was mostly not a mapping problem.

## Where it started

**614** microbedecoder records, **540 MAPPED**, **74 at NEEDS_EXPERT with zero occurrences**. Not one of the 74 is used in any medium; they came from a label list, not from recipes. And `NEEDS_EXPERT` implied a curator would one day find an ontology term for `Formate+methanol` — none exists and none could, because a combination is not a substance.

## What was already curated and never applied

`mappings/microbedecoder_residual_research_decomposition.tsv` holds **42 curated decompositions** with a `component_curies` column, produced by the research pass. **Nothing ever wrote them into the records.** The file sat as a mapping artefact while the records it describes stayed unresolved.

I initially derived my own decomposition by splitting labels on `+` before finding it. The curated column is strictly better and supersedes that:

- it resolves constituents a split cannot — `CMC + PY + Horse Serum` splits into a literal `PY` that resolves to nothing, where the curated row expands it to peptone + yeast extract; likewise `Corn Steep Liquor` → `cas:66071-94-1`, `3-methyl mercaptopropionate` → `CHEBI:1438`
- it covers labels with **no composition to split on** — `PYG`, `PYGS`, `GYPS`, `PYEG`, `BHI` are abbreviations, and the curated expansions are the only route to blends-of-ingredients

## Three treatments

**Decomposed (42)** — minted under the #288 convention with constituents in `components`. **First use of that slot**, which had been in the schema unused at 0 records; its contract is "populate only from a verifiable recipe source", satisfied by the curated file. No concentrations recorded, because no row states one.

**Media cross-referenced to CultureMech** via `culturemech_medium_name` — also previously unused — and **verified by composition, not by name**, since fuzzy name matching is what put `KF` on `Lys-Phe`:

    BHI  -> CultureMech:015492   Beef heart + Calf brains + Proteose Peptone IS brain heart infusion
    GYPS -> CultureMech:002799   name exact, 3 of 4 constituents agree

**Only 2 of 12 survive that check**, and the rejections are the point: `Modified Cooked Meat Medium` matches `cooked_meat_medium`, which is the **un**modified one; `Fastidious Anaerobe Broth **With Meat Granules**` matches a broth with no meat granules; `PYG` is ambiguous across **six** CultureMech variants. The other seven have no CultureMech medium at all.

**Repaired (4)** — comma splits rejoined:

    Butane-1 + 4-diol                       -> butane-1,4-diol            CHEBI:41189
    Ethylenediamine-N + N'-disuccinic Acid  -> EDDS                       minted (no ChEBI term)
    2-tetrachloroethane                     -> 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane  CHEBI:36026
    Sulfonamide                             -> CHEBI:35358 (exact label; was PENDING_REVIEW)

## Result

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| microbedecoder MAPPED | 540 | **593** |
| ungrounded | 74 | **21** |
| records using `components` | 0 | **49** |

## What remains, and why it is not curation

**21 records, all zero-occurrence.** `0129 (2` + `4-Diamino-6` are two thirds of `O/129 (2,4-diamino-6,7-diisopropylpteridine)` — the third fragment is not in the corpus, so the label cannot be reconstructed and guessing would invent a compound. `PY-cellobiose`/`-fructose`/`-maltose`/`-pectin` follow the curated `PY-glucose-rumen Fluid` pattern and could be decomposed the same way. `Sugars`, `Mono- And Disaccharides` are category labels, not ingredients.

## Verification

SSSOM Rules A/B1/B2/B3 · reconcile 0 gap/orphan/stale · flat exports fresh · `validate-strict` 0 errors · **#352 filename-case guard** (which fired correctly on the relabels) · 923 tests.

items.title: Re-ground four records that asserted an unrelated molecule (#263)
items.body:
Closes #263. These were surfaced by #261, which found the plausibility gate had been checking a column that could never fail it.

## The errors

Each record carried the **correct CAS-RN** while asserting a CHEBI id for a different substance — and each had `molecular_formula`/`inchi`/`smiles` auto-backfilled *from the wrong term* by `AUTO_BACKFILL_CHEBI_CHEMISTRY`, so the error had already propagated well past the id field.

| record | asserted | what that id actually is |
|---|---|---|
| Casamino acids | CHEBI:78020 | **heptacosanoate**, a C27 fatty acid |
| Na2S2O4 | CHEBI:61278 | **scutellarin**, a flavone glucuronide |
| Sodium succinate dibasic | CHEBI:150903 | a trisaccharide glycoside |
| Tomatidine hydrochloride | CHEBI:93130 | a triazinane-trione |

The blast radius is the part worth noting: `Casamino acids` had also been **reclassified from `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE` to `SINGLE_INGREDIENT`** — by a rule that fires when chemical structure is populated — purely because heptacosanoate's structure had been written onto it. A wrong grounding silently rewrote the record's type.

## The re-groundings

- **Casamino acids → FOODON:03315719** *mammalian milk protein (hydrolyzed)*. It is an acid hydrolysate of casein, an undefined peptide/amino-acid mixture. Same term as the sibling `Casein_Peptone` record, which is the same class of hydrolysate. `ingredient_type` restored to `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE`.
- **Na2S2O4 → CHEBI:66870** *sodium dithionite*. The label's element multiset (Na₂S₂O₄) matches the term's formula `2Na.O4S2` exactly, so this one is now formula-verified rather than lexical.
- **Sodium succinate dibasic → `cas:150-90-3`**, narrowMatch to **CHEBI:15741** *succinic acid*. ChEBI has no disodium succinate entry (checked against the OAK sqlite), so this takes the established `cas:` identifier pattern already used by 248 records (MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md Section 3).
- **Tomatidine hydrochloride** — the `cas:69004-03-1` identifier was already correct; only the bogus narrowMatch parent moved, to **CHEBI:9629** *tomatidine*, the actual free base.

The backfilled chemistry is **dropped, not recomputed**. Deriving formula/InChI/SMILES belongs to the enrichment pass; leaving a wrong formula in place is worse than leaving the field absent. Correct CAS-RNs are retained on all four.

## Verification

- `just validate-strict` → **0 ERROR rows** (2883 files)
- `just validate-products` → **exit 0**; `IMPLAUSIBLE_LABEL` 61 → 59
- `just sync-curated` + `just export-lists` to regenerate collections and `docs/data/` products; `reconcile_sssom.py --apply` synced the 4 stale SSSOM rows
- Full suite: **696 pass**. The single failure, `test_check_chebi_currency.py::test_kgmicrobe_default_is_a_sibling_not_a_hardcoded_home`, is **pre-existing and unrelated** — it asserts `"/Users/"` is absent from a resolved path, which fails for any checkout under `/Users/`, and it fails identically on `main`.

## Two remain flagged, correctly

`Casamino acids` → *mammalian milk protein (hydrolyzed)* and `Sodium succinate dibasic` → *succinic acid* still report `IMPLAUSIBLE_LABEL`, because the labels share no content word with the canonical form (`succinate` vs `succinic`). These are now **verified-correct groundings the lexical heuristic cannot see** — the same class as `Soy peptone` → *vegetable protein, hydrolyzed*, which the validator's own comment cites as the canonical example. They belong to the `exceptions` triage batch in #261 rather than to this PR, so they are deliberately left in the queue rather than waived one-off.

items.title: Four verified wrong CHEBI groundings the no-op plausibility gate was hiding
items.body:
Surfaced by pointing the plausibility gate at the curator label (#261). These are **not** naming-convention noise — each is a record asserting a CHEBI id for an unrelated molecule, verified against live `sqlite:obo:chebi`.

| record | asserted id | what the id actually is | what the ingredient is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Casamino_Acids.yaml` | CHEBI:78020 | **heptacosanoate** (C27 fatty acid anion) | acid-hydrolysed casein digest — a peptide/amino-acid mixture |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Na2s2o4.yaml` | CHEBI:61278 | **scutellarin** (a flavone glucuronide) | sodium dithionite, Na₂S₂O₄ — a reducing agent |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Sodium_Succinate_Dibasic.yaml` | CHEBI:150903 | a trisaccharide-type glycoside (`(2S,3S,4R,5S,6S)-2-[…]oxane-3,4,5-triol`) | disodium succinate |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Tomatidine_Hydrochloride.yaml` | CHEBI:93130 | `1-methyl-3-[…]-1,3,5-triazinane-2,4,6-trione` | tomatidine HCl, a steroidal alkaloid |

`Casamino acids → heptacosanoate` and `Na2S2O4 → scutellarin` are the starkest: nothing about either pair is chemically close, and both are common media ingredients, so the wrong id propagates into every export and downstream KG edge.

## Also worth a look (different failure class)

`Fructooligosaccharides (FOS)` → CHEBI:28645 **beta-D-fructofuranose**. Not an unrelated molecule, but a **granularity** error: a single monosaccharide standing in for an oligosaccharide mixture. Closer to the #237/#216 `DEFINED_MEDIUM` discussion than to the four above.

## Scope note

The gate reported 61 `IMPLAUSIBLE_LABEL` in total. **Most of the rest look like correct groundings** the lexical heuristic cannot see — `2-Furfuraldehyde` → *furfural*, `Irgasan` → *triclosan*, `Sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate` → *Mesna*, `Soy peptone` → *vegetable protein, hydrolyzed* (the very example the validator's own comment cites as a legitimate no-shared-word case). So the 61 is a **triage queue, not a defect count**, which is exactly why #261 holds this surface at `severity: warn` rather than flipping it to `error`.

These four, though, are confirmed and should be re-grounded.

Related: #261, #114.

items.title: In-session (Claude) role curation: role coverage 43.2% → 47.5%
items.body:
## Summary
Pushes functional-role coverage past 43% via **in-session Claude curation** — I (the model) assigned roles directly, no external API call/key. Targets the 163 role-less MAPPED records with occurrence ≥ 2 that the deterministic synonym / CHEBI-ancestry / name-list passes couldn't reach; **79 high-confidence assignments** applied.

**Coverage: 43.2% → 47.5% of mapped records** (887 records, 968 roles).

### What was assigned (unambiguous chemistry only)
- **TRACE_ELEMENT** — Co/Ni/Fe/V/Mo/Ce/Cr/W/B salts + trace-element solutions
- **ELECTRON_DONOR** — thiosulfate, tetrathionate
- **REDUCING_AGENT** — dithionite, (meta)bisulfite
- **ELECTRON_ACCEPTOR** — tetrachloroethene, perchlorate, nitrous oxide
- **BUFFER** — mono/dibasic phosphates, glycylglycine, HOMOPIPES, maleate
- **CARBON_SOURCE** — hydrocarbons (hexadecane, HMN, isopropanol) + aromatic degradation substrates (benzoates, catechol, phenol, m-xylene, cinnamate, vanillate, …) + trimethylamine
- **SURFACTANT** — Tween 40/60, tyloxapol, glycerol mono-esters
- **PH/REDOX_INDICATOR** — bromothymol/bromocresol; TTC, methylene blue
- **COFACTOR_PROVIDER** — haemin, CoA, NAD, coenzyme M
- **VITAMIN_SOURCE** — PABA · **NITROGEN_SOURCE** — urea, ammonium salts · **PROTEIN_SOURCE** — serum · **SELECTIVE_AGENT** — crystal violet, cycloheximide

### Deliberately skipped (ambiguous / no clean enum)
Nucleosides & nucleobases, osmolytes (betaine, ectoine, choline), NaOH (pH adjuster), soils/seawater, enzymes (catalase), Fe(III)/Mn(IV) minerals (context-dependent acceptor vs source), fatty-acid soaps.

### Quality gates
- Every assignment is **PROVISIONAL** (confidence 0.6, `COMPUTATIONAL_PREDICTION`, curator `claude_in_session_curation`) — easy to find, review, revert.
- Extended `audit_role_plausibility` tokens (S2O4/S2O5, aminobenzo, serum) so the plausibility CI gate recognises the new legit names. **Audit: 0 flags.**
- `validate_strict`: 0 errors / 2274 files · full suite: **314 passed**.

items.title: Verify MICRO:0000520 (clarified rumen fluid) before applying microbedecoder residual decomposition
items.body:
From the review of PR #202 (deep-research groundings for the microbedecoder residual).

Six of the seven "repo convention" biological/complex CURIEs asserted in `mappings/microbedecoder_residual_research_decomposition.tsv` are confirmed already used in `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` (Trypticase peptone MICRO:0000175, casitone MICRO:0000606, horse serum MICRO:0001235, carboxymethylcellulose CHEBI:85146, meat-cooked FOODON:03305103, D-gluconate CHEBI:18391).

**The exception: `MICRO:0000520` "clarified rumen fluid" appears in zero repo records.** It is used in three proposed decomposition rows (`PY-glucose-rumen Fluid`, `PYG + Rumen Fluid`, `Casitone + Yeast Extract + Rumen Fluid`) and one complex-medium row (`Fermented Rumen Extract`). The research agent already flagged rumen fluid as having no exact term and recommended it as a `broadMatch` only, but the specific CURIE was not independently confirmed against OLS/MICRO.

**Action before applying:** confirm `MICRO:0000520` exists in the MICRO ontology and is labelled "clarified rumen fluid" (or find the correct term / UBERON:0010228 ruminal fluid), and decide whether to mint a `kgmicrobe.compound:`/placeholder for rumen fluid as the report's next-steps section suggests. Same open question applies to corn steep liquor (no FOODON/CHEBI term) and the TYGVS VFA mixture.

Related: #200 (chebi.db accession-ceiling refresh, which unblocks the 6 out-of-coverage antibiotics in the same PR).

items.title: Role QA audit + fix 2 implausible mis-tags + add ENERGY_SOURCE dimension
items.body:
## Summary
Two follow-ups: a quick QA fix that defends the existing roles, and an additive ENERGY_SOURCE dimension.

### 1. Role QA audit + fixes
New `audit_role_plausibility.py` flags `media_role` assignments whose ingredient name matches none of the plausible-name tokens for its **narrow-definition** role (BUFFER/SOLIDIFYING/REDUCING/CHELATOR/VITAMIN/AMINO_ACID/PROTEIN — CARBON/MINERAL span too many chemical classes to audit by name). It surfaced exactly two genuine mis-tags, both fixed:
- **`MgSO4·7H2O`** was tagged `BUFFER` from a bad CultureMech source synonym — MgSO4 is a mineral salt, not a buffer. Dropped (MINERAL retained).
- **`EDTA (acid form)`** was tagged `AMINO_ACID_SOURCE` — the broad CHEBI "amino acid" ancestry rule over-matched this polyamino-carboxylic **chelator**; re-tagged `CHELATOR`.

The other audit flags were all genuine (non-proteinogenic amino acids like GABA/sarcosine/canavanine; acetate-as-buffer; sulfite-as-reductant) — the token lists were completed to recognize them. A new **`test_role_plausibility.py`** asserts the curated data has zero implausible roles, so this can't regress.

### 2. ENERGY_SOURCE dimension
`infer_energy_source.py` adds `ENERGY_SOURCE` as a second role to records already holding `CARBON_SOURCE` that match a tight textbook energy-substrate set (glycolytic/TCA acids, common fermentable sugars, ethanol/glycerol). Non-metabolizable analogs (2-deoxy-/3-O-methyl-glucose), sugar phosphates and fatty-acid esters are excluded so the role stays meaningful. **+78 roles; multi-role records 4 → 81.**

## Validation
- `validate_strict.py`: **0 errors / 2274 files**
- `validate_roles.py`: **889 roles, 0 errors**; plausibility audit: **0 flags**
- Full suite: **308 passed**
